text: Photonic-crystal defect cavities reach the highest Purcell factors in solid-state photonics because they combine ultra-high Q with:
choices: A very large mode volume that spreads light over many wavelengths
A metallic mirror coating around the defect
An ultra-small mode volume on the order of (lambda/n)^3
explanation: The Purcell factor scales as Q/V, so an ultra-small mode volume ~(lambda/n)^3 combined with Q > 10^6 gives F_P ~ 10^4-10^5. A large mode volume would reduce the Purcell factor; the cavity uses the dielectric bandgap rather than metal mirrors, and it works at room temperature.
